subtitle: Learn to recognize the protected characteristics under the Minnesota Human Rights Act, consider the setting where a concern arises and use the proper process to raise it.
scope: An introductory staff course on selected Minnesota Human Rights Act protections relevant to employment and public services, with a comparison to public accommodations. It is not a complete guide to every chapter provision, exception, legal claim or filing deadline. Practice cases teach recognition and responsible next steps; actual interpretation and decisions follow authorized procedures.
introTranscript: The Minnesota Human Rights Act prohibits specified discriminatory practices in different areas of life. Protected classes describe characteristics or statuses the law addresses; they are not a list of people who deserve respect while others do not. The setting matters. Employment, public services and public accommodations do not use identical lists or requirements. In this course, you will recognize the relevant characteristics, distinguish those settings, use definitions carefully and respond to a concern without making a legal finding yourself. You will also distinguish the statute from state workplace policy. Practice with practice cases at your own pace, and use the direct sources and appropriate agency process for actual work.

lessons.title: Understand what a protected class means
lessons.summary: Use the term without dividing people into those who matter and those who do not.
lessons.objective: Explain a protected class as a characteristic or status addressed by a legal or policy provision.
objectives: Explain a protected class as a characteristic or status addressed by a legal or policy provision.
Distinguish recognizing a concern from establishing a violation.
Identify why the setting and applicable provision matter.
takeaways: Protected classes describe characteristics or statuses addressed by a provision.
A course activity cannot determine a legal violation.
lessons.statement: Recognize the characteristic, the conduct and the setting before drawing a conclusion.

image.caption: A presenter points to a whiteboard chart while two colleagues discuss it at a table.

intro.heading: The term points to a protection, not a personal ranking
intro.body:
A protected class is a characteristic or status that an applicable law or policy addresses in its prohibition of discrimination. Race, religion and disability are examples. The term does not mean that only some people deserve respect or that a person must belong to a small or historically disadvantaged group before any protection can apply. The relevant provision, setting and facts determine the actual question.

The Minnesota Human Rights Act describes unfair discriminatory practices in different settings, including employment, public services and public accommodations. These settings have distinct language and protected-class lists. A list copied from one section is not a reliable substitute for checking the provision relevant to the work. Other laws and agency policies may also apply. Staff should recognize the issue without assuming this short course contains every legal requirement.

In a practice case, a staff member hears a statement connecting a hiring decision to an applicant’s religion. The statement raises an employment concern that needs the proper process. The learner does not need to prove a legal case before reporting a concern through an applicable route, but should not declare a final finding based on a classroom scenario. Accurate information about what was said and the decision involved is more useful than a label about the speaker’s identity or motives.

Keep the person and the concern distinct. People can share several characteristics, and the relevance of one may depend on the particular decision. Do not ask a colleague to disclose personal information to become an example for the course. Use practice material for learning. In actual work, follow the appropriate reporting, information and decision procedures, including any responsibilities assigned to your role.

lessons.keyStatement: Recognizing a possible concern supports the proper process; it does not settle the case.

flashcards.back: A characteristic or status addressed by an applicable nondiscrimination provision.
The area of activity, such as employment or public services, relevant to the provision.
Information suggesting a question that should be addressed through the appropriate process.
A determination reached through the authorized process, not by a course answer key.

items.title: Respect
items.body: A protected-class list is not a permission to treat others poorly. State workplace policy and broader equity practice also matter. The learning question is which protection and procedure applies, not which person is worthy of consideration.

items.title: Context
items.body: Employment and public-service access can involve the same individual in different roles. A colleague’s job assignment is an employment issue; their use of a public program is a different setting. Identify the action before selecting the source.

items.title: Evidence
items.body: Describe the actual words or action, its context and relevant decision. Do not invent motive or decide membership from appearance. A concern can be reported without the learner claiming to have established every legal element.

tabs.heading: Three ways to describe a concern

tabs.label: Specific conduct
tabs.body: The practice comment connected religion to hiring describes the material at issue. This helps the appropriate process examine the concern without demanding that the learner make a final legal determination.

tabs.label: Identity guess
tabs.body: Guessing a person’s religion from their clothing does not establish it and does not provide a sound analysis of the decision. Avoid unnecessary personal inference and use the observable conduct relevant to the concern.

tabs.label: Universal verdict
tabs.body: Every disagreement is illegal discrimination ignores the setting, facts and requirements. A disagreement may involve respectful-workplace questions or legitimate work direction. Use the applicable process rather than a sweeping classroom verdict.

check.question: Which description is the most accurate starting point?
check.correct: The practice comment links religion to a hiring choice and raises a concern for the appropriate process.
wrong: The speaker’s appearance proves their motive.
Only members of a numerical minority have any protected-class rights.
A learning answer establishes a final legal violation.
check.feedbackCorrect: This identifies the characteristic, decision and need for the proper process without an unsupported finding.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Protection depends on the applicable provision and circumstances, not a personal ranking or appearance. A course can teach recognition and responsible action; it cannot adjudicate a real complaint.

sorting.heading: Meaning, useful concern or unsupported claim?

items.text: Protected class names a characteristic or status addressed by a provision.
The setting identifies which activity is being examined.
Describe a statement that linked religion to the practice hiring decision.
Use the appropriate process without declaring a final finding.
A person’s appearance establishes their belief and motive.
A completed learning check proves a real legal violation.

lessons.next: Next, examine the employer protected-class list and state workplace policy.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A colleague asks whether protected class means only certain people deserve respectful treatment.
options: It identifies protections in particular provisions; everyone should be treated respectfully, and the actual setting matters.
It ranks whose concerns are important.
It gives permission to mistreat anyone not named in one copied list.
responses: This explains the term while preserving respect and context.
The term is not a ranking of people or experiences.
A list is not a license for mistreatment, and one section does not describe every applicable protection.

lessons.transfer: Describe a practice concern by its conduct, characteristic and setting, without a legal verdict.

move.control: You can recognize a question without guessing identities or deciding a case.
move.failure: A label replaces the actual conduct, setting and proper process.
move.next: Use a practice example and identify the relevant activity.

lessons.title: Recognize employment protections and workplace-policy differences
lessons.summary: Read the employer list in context and avoid treating a policy list as the statute itself.
lessons.objective: Identify characteristics listed in the Act’s employer provision.
objectives: Identify characteristics listed in the Act’s employer provision.
Explain that MMB 1436 has its own workplace-policy list.
Distinguish job-related decisions from a classroom determination of an exception.
takeaways: The Act’s employer provision names specific characteristics and statuses.
State policy and the statute are related but distinct sources.
Staff should not improvise legal exceptions to justify a decision.
lessons.statement: Use the applicable source and the authorized employment process.

image.caption: A presenter points to a whiteboard chart while two colleagues discuss it at a table.

intro.heading: Employment requires attention to the actual provision
intro.body:
The employer provision in Minnesota Statutes 363A.08, subdivision 2, addresses race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, gender identity, marital status, status with regard to public assistance, familial status, membership or activity in a local commission, disability, sexual orientation and age. It covers specified hiring, discharge and employment decisions. The section includes conditions and exemptions that require proper interpretation; this course does not authorize staff to make those determinations on their own.

State workplace policy is a related source with its own language. MMB Policy 1436 also names gender expression and, for employees, genetic information. Do not describe these policy entries as though the employer list in 363A.08 uses identical wording. The policy prohibits protected-class harassment and discrimination in the workplace or public-service environment and provides reporting routes and role responsibilities. Its specific definitions and scope matter.

In a practice hiring discussion, an employee suggests that an applicant’s marital status shows whether they will stay in the job. That is an assumption about a protected status, not evidence of a job qualification. A staff member should describe the concern and use the applicable process rather than invent a rule about what people with that status will do. Use approved job-related criteria and the responsible employment procedures for actual work.

A statutory exception cannot be converted into a casual team preference. The Act includes bona fide occupational qualification language and other provisions, but merely calling a preference business related does not establish that an exception applies. Obtain the appropriate authorized guidance. This learning activity builds recognition and careful wording; it does not complete a hiring review, decide an accommodation request or determine whether a particular decision is lawful.

lessons.keyStatement: A copied label or informal preference cannot substitute for the actual employment requirements.

flashcards.back: The part of 363A.08 describing specified discriminatory employer practices.
A statutory status with a defined scope that includes specified family and care situations.
A legally defined local human-rights body; membership or activity appears in the employer list.
A difference in wording, scope or responsibilities between a statute and agency policy.

items.title: Listed statuses
items.body: The employer provision includes public-assistance status, familial status and local-commission membership or activity. These can be missed by an informal summary limited to a few familiar categories. Use the direct list for the relevant setting.

items.title: Additional policy wording
items.body: Policy 1436 lists gender expression and genetic information for employees. This course identifies them as policy protections rather than adding words to the employer statute. In actual work, other applicable laws and policies may also matter.

items.title: Exceptions
items.body: Exceptions depend on the applicable law and facts. A learner should not declare that a customer preference or a team’s habit creates one. Refer actual questions to the authorized employment and legal process while preserving reporting responsibilities.

tabs.label: Job evidence
tabs.body: Use the approved qualification and evidence of the applicant’s relevant experience. A consistent job-related process helps focus the discussion, but does not by itself certify the entire selection as lawful or equitable.

tabs.label: Status assumption
tabs.body: The assumption about marital status predicts loyalty from personal status. Identify the statement and the hiring decision involved. Do not replace it with a favorable stereotype about a different status.

tabs.label: Authorized review
tabs.body: A concern about the discussion belongs in the appropriate agency process. Staff do not need to create a legal argument before using a reporting route, and course feedback cannot approve or overturn an actual employment decision.

check.question: Which statement preserves the distinction between the statute and state policy?
check.correct: The employer provision has its listed classes; Policy 1436 additionally names gender expression and employee genetic information.
wrong: Every list in every source uses identical words.
An informal team preference establishes a legal exception.
Marital status reliably predicts an applicant’s commitment.
check.feedbackCorrect: This identifies the sources accurately and keeps their wording distinct.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Different sources can provide related protections with different wording and conditions. Personal-status stereotypes and informal preferences are not substitutes for job evidence or an authorized interpretation of exceptions.

sorting.heading: Employer list, policy distinction or unsupported employment claim?

items.text: Membership or activity in a local commission appears in 363A.08 subdivision 2.
Familial status appears in the employer provision.
Policy 1436 names gender expression.
Policy 1436 includes genetic information for employees.
A team preference automatically establishes a statutory exception.
Marital status tells the team who will stay employed.

lessons.next: Next, distinguish public-service access from public accommodations.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: Someone says a hiring preference based on marital status is fine because the team believes it predicts retention.
options: Identify the status-based concern and use the proper process and job-related criteria rather than accepting the stereotype.
Adopt it as an exception without review.
Replace it with a preference for a different marital status.
responses: This recognizes the concern and preserves authorized employment responsibilities.
An informal belief does not establish an applicable legal exception.
Reversing the preference does not solve the unsupported status-based reasoning.

lessons.transfer: Identify a practice employment concern and the source distinction that matters, without deciding the case.

move.control: You can recognize the relevant employment list and policy wording.
move.failure: An informal preference is treated as permission to make a status-based decision.
move.next: Review the practice statement and identify a responsible next process.

lessons.title: Match the protection to the service setting
lessons.summary: Compare public services with public accommodations without inventing a universal list.
lessons.objective: Identify the protected-class list in 363A.12 subdivision 1.
objectives: Identify the protected-class list in 363A.12 subdivision 1.
Distinguish a public service from a public accommodation using the statutory definitions.
Explain why a missing entry in one list does not settle every applicable protection.
takeaways: Public services and public accommodations are separate statutory settings.
Other applicable laws and policies may also govern the actual concern.
lessons.statement: Identify the activity before using a protected-class list.

image.caption: A presenter points to a whiteboard chart while two colleagues discuss it at a table.

intro.heading: Service context matters
intro.body:
Minnesota Statutes 363A.12, subdivision 1, prohibits specified discrimination in access to, admission to, use of or benefit from a public service because of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, disability, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation or status with regard to public assistance. It also contains disability physical and program access provisions with stated conditions. Staff should not summarize those conditions as a general option to deny access whenever an adjustment is inconvenient. Actual access questions require the appropriate authorized review and other applicable requirements.

The Act defines a public service by its connection to a Minnesota state or local public facility, department, agency or other listed public body. Public accommodations are defined separately around facilities or businesses whose goods or services are made available to the public. The public-accommodations list in 363A.11 includes marital status and does not use the same public-assistance-status entry as 363A.12. The terms should not be selected casually because both involve members of the public.

In a practice service discussion, someone says a person receiving public assistance should not be welcomed at a public information service because of that status. That raises a concern connected to the public-services provision and relevant agency policy. It is different from applying the authorized eligibility requirements of a specific benefit program. Staff should identify the statement, service and decision, then use the proper process instead of improvising either an exclusion or an eligibility waiver.

A characteristic absent from one section’s list is not automatically unprotected under every law or policy. The actual activity may involve other provisions, federal requirements or state workplace policy. Recognize the question, verify the relevant sources and seek the proper guidance. This course provides a selected comparison, not an exhaustive determination of coverage.

lessons.keyStatement: A setting-specific list is a starting point for the applicable inquiry, not every source’s final word.

flashcards.back: A state or local public facility, department, agency or other body within the Act’s definition.
A separately defined facility or business offering goods, services or facilities to the public.
A statutory status concerning receipt of specified assistance or subsidies.
A question about which provision and conditions govern the actual activity.

items.title: The actual activity
items.body: Describe whether the decision concerns employment, a public program or another activity. An agency can act as an employer and deliver a public service. The same organization name does not eliminate the need to identify which conduct is being examined.

items.title: Different lists
items.body: Marital status appears in the public-accommodations list, while public-assistance status appears in the public-services list. These examples show why copying an employment list into every setting can mislead. Check the full relevant provision and other applicable sources.

items.title: Eligibility and access
items.body: A benefit program may have authorized eligibility requirements. Their existence does not authorize stereotypes or inventing an exclusion based on status. Do not waive requirements yourself or assume that every access question is already answered by an eligibility label.

tabs.label: Source-based
tabs.body: The practice exclusion concerns a public service and public-assistance status, so the relevant provision and policy need to be used. This identifies a question for the proper process without a final legal finding.

tabs.label: Copied list
tabs.body: The employment list may include classes not identically named in the service section. Copying it into a service note can misstate the legal source. Use the appropriate provision and seek authorized interpretation for actual work.

tabs.label: No protection anywhere
tabs.body: Concluding that a missing list entry means no protection under any source goes beyond the comparison. Other laws, policy or another setting may matter. Recognize the limit instead of using it as permission to disregard the concern.

check.question: What is the sound way to use the lists?
check.correct: Identify the activity, read the relevant provision and consider other applicable law or policy through the proper process.
wrong: Use the employment list as the only list for every public service.
Treat a missing entry in one section as proof there is no protection anywhere.
Decide an access exception informally whenever the team finds it inconvenient.
check.feedbackCorrect: This keeps context and applicable sources visible without inventing a universal conclusion.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The lists differ, and access conditions or other protections cannot be decided by a shortcut. Use the correct provision and authorized procedures rather than a copied list or an informal exception.

sorting.heading: Public service, public accommodation or unsupported shortcut?

items.text: 363A.12 subdivision 1 lists public-assistance status.
363A.12 contains physical and program access language.
363A.11 subdivision 1 lists marital status.
363A.11 concerns a separately defined place of public accommodation.
Every protected-class list is identical.
A missing entry means no other protection can apply.

lessons.next: Next, use the chapter’s definitions without guessing personal characteristics.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A team copies an employer protected-class list into a public-service explanation and says it covers every relevant law.
options: Identify the public-service provision accurately and state that actual questions may require other applicable sources.
Keep the copied list because all settings have the same requirements.
Delete every protection that was not in the first summary.
responses: This repairs the source and preserves the inquiry’s scope.
The statute uses distinct lists and conditions.
A short summary cannot determine that other protections do not exist.

lessons.transfer: Compare a practice employment and service question and identify the appropriate statutory setting for each.

move.control: You can choose a setting-specific source and preserve its limits.
move.failure: A copied list becomes an unsupported coverage conclusion.
move.next: Practice using 363A.08 and 363A.12 for their different settings.

lessons.title: Read definitions without making assumptions about people
lessons.summary: Use selected definitions carefully and avoid inferring identity from appearance.
lessons.objective: Describe selected chapter definitions with their relevant scope.
objectives: Describe selected chapter definitions with their relevant scope.
Explain that identity and status may not be visible.
Separate recognition of a definition from permission to collect personal information.
takeaways: Statutory definitions can be broader or more specific than everyday usage.
Appearance does not establish identity, status or individual needs.
Learning a definition does not authorize collecting personal information.
lessons.statement: Use definitions to improve the inquiry, not to categorize people by guesswork.

image.caption: A presenter points to a whiteboard chart while two colleagues discuss it at a table.

intro.heading: Definitions matter to the actual question
intro.body:
The Human Rights Act defines terms for use within the chapter. Those definitions help explain why an everyday assumption can be incomplete. For example, race includes traits associated with race, including hair texture and hairstyles such as braids, locs and twists. Sex includes pregnancy, childbirth and disabilities related to pregnancy or childbirth. These definitions should be read with the applicable provision rather than reduced to what someone thinks a category looks like.

Other definitions also need attention to scope. Familial status includes specified relationships involving minors and specified care situations involving people unable to meet essential requirements or make necessary decisions. In employment cases, marital status includes protection concerning the identity, circumstances, actions or beliefs of a spouse or former spouse. The course does not supply a decision about whether an actual person’s circumstances meet every condition. Use the direct source and proper process for that question.

Gender identity and sexual orientation are distinct terms, and neither should be assumed from someone’s appearance. Disability under the chapter includes specified impairments, a record of an impairment, being regarded as having an impairment and certain episodic or remitting impairments. A visible sign is not required for every defined condition, and staff should not diagnose a person from a course scenario.

Understanding a definition does not give permission to gather personal information. In the practice, use only the details supplied. In real work, information collection and use must have the appropriate purpose, authority and procedure, including specific employment and accommodation requirements where relevant. Do not question a colleague to prove that they belong to a class for the sake of a learning activity. Describe the conduct and setting, recognize the question and use the appropriate process.

inThisLesson: Keep personal information within its proper process.
lessons.keyStatement: Definitions guide understanding; they do not authorize identity guessing or unnecessary disclosure.

flashcards.back: The chapter includes traits associated with race, including specified hair textures and hairstyles.
The chapter includes pregnancy, childbirth and disabilities related to them.
The chapter describes a person’s inherent sense of gender, which may not be visible.
The boundary between understanding a term and determining its application to an actual case.

items.title: Family and care
items.body: Familial status is not limited to the phrase parent of a young child. The chapter contains specified minor and care relationships. Read those conditions rather than deciding an actual situation from an informal label or an incomplete classroom summary.

items.title: Disability
items.body: The definition includes a record, perceived impairment and specified episodic or remitting conditions. Do not demand a visible sign or diagnose an individual. Actual accommodation requests and information handling have their own appropriate process and responsible roles.

items.title: Identity and appearance
items.body: The statutory gender-identity definition expressly recognizes that it may not be visible. A hairstyle, name, voice or clothing choice does not allow the learner to establish every identity or personal circumstance. Focus on the conduct and source rather than guesses.

tabs.label: Source check
tabs.body: A practice comment about hairstyles can be reviewed with the race definition and applicable setting. This helps identify a possible concern without making a final case determination.

tabs.label: Personal inference
tabs.body: Guessing orientation or gender identity from appearance confuses observation with a personal conclusion. Avoid assigning labels and do not make a colleague provide information to satisfy a classroom exercise.

tabs.label: Proper process
tabs.body: An actual question about status, coverage or accommodation should use authorized information and the relevant procedures. A learner’s awareness of the definition is useful preparation, not permission to conduct an improvised inquiry into private circumstances.

check.question: Which statement accurately uses a chapter definition?
check.correct: Race includes traits associated with race, including hair texture and specified hairstyles; the actual concern still needs its applicable setting and process.
wrong: Gender identity is always visible in clothing.
Every disability must be visible before a concern can be raised.
Knowing a definition permits any staff member to demand personal proof.
check.feedbackCorrect: This uses the statutory definition while preserving the application and information limits.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Appearance is not a reliable basis for assigning identity or disability, and definitions do not create data-collection authority. Keep the concern specific and use the proper process for actual questions.

sorting.heading: Definition, careful use or unsupported inference?

items.text: Race includes specified traits associated with race.
Sex includes pregnancy and childbirth.
Check familial-status conditions in the direct source.
Use practice information rather than demanding a colleague’s disclosure.
Clothing establishes a person’s gender identity.
A disability is irrelevant unless it is visible.

lessons.next: Next, use the appropriate reporting process and preserve protection against reprisal.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A learner wants to ask a colleague private questions so the class can determine which protected class they belong to.
scenario.prompt: What is a better learning choice?
options: Use the practice case and the source definitions without demanding personal disclosure.
Require the colleague to explain every personal status.
Assign the colleague an identity from appearance.
responses: This keeps the activity relevant and avoids an unsupported personal inquiry.
The learning exercise does not authorize unnecessary disclosure.
Appearance cannot establish the personal definitions or actual coverage.

lessons.transfer: Explain a selected definition and one limit on its use in a practice situation.

move.control: You can read the term carefully without categorizing real people by inference.
move.failure: Definitions become a reason for unnecessary personal questioning.
move.next: Use the practice details and identify the relevant source definition.

lessons.title: Respond to a concern through the appropriate process
lessons.summary: Distinguish employee reporting options, manager duties and protection against retaliation.
objectives: Distinguish employee encouragement from immediate manager and supervisor reporting duties.
Recognize reprisal and retaliation concerns without adjudicating them.
takeaways: A concern can use the proper route before the learner makes a legal finding.
Managers and supervisors have distinct immediate reporting duties under 1436.
Opposition, reports and participation should not be punished or discouraged.
lessons.statement: Take the concern seriously and preserve the responsibilities of the applicable process.

image.caption: A presenter points to a whiteboard chart while two colleagues discuss it at a table.

intro.heading: Reporting is a process, not a classroom verdict
intro.body:
Knowing protected classes helps staff recognize when a concern may belong in a formal process. It does not require a learner to decide a legal case before reporting. MMB Policy 1436 strongly encourages employees and relevant third parties to report protected-class harassment or discrimination, whether they received the conduct, observed it or otherwise know about it. Its listed options include agency managers or supervisors, the agency Affirmative Action Officer, HR and agency management. The policy also identifies an option when a report concerns an agency head.

Managers and supervisors have a different responsibility. They must immediately report allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to HR or the agency AAO and follow agency complaint and investigation procedures. A supportive conversation, a learning exercise or a consultant appointment cannot replace or delay that duty. Authorized investigation responsibilities remain with assigned roles under agency procedures. The course does not create a blanket prohibition on managers performing duties assigned through those procedures.

The Act’s reprisal provision and Policy 1436’s non-retaliation language protect specified opposition, reporting and participation. A practice reduction in opportunities following a report can raise a concern to examine; timing alone does not establish every fact or legal element. Do not label every work change a reprisal, but do not dismiss a concern or pressure a person to withdraw a report. Use the applicable process with accurate information.

Keep actual reports and records in their proper channels. Do not post allegations in a course discussion or promise secrecy beyond the process. Sexual-harassment concerns have the separate Policy 1329 route and requirements. This lesson introduces responsible recognition and distinctions, not a complete reporting manual or a replacement for agency procedures.

lessons.keyStatement: Use the applicable procedure without replacing it with informal learning or consultation.

flashcards.back: A route provided by the applicable policy for raising a concern.
A distinct immediate HR or AAO reporting responsibility under Policy 1436.
A question about adverse or discouraging conduct connected to protected opposition, reporting or participation.
An inquiry conducted by authorized roles under the agency’s procedures.

items.title: Employee choice
items.body: Policy 1436 encourages reports through several listed agency routes. An employee does not need to obtain a consultant’s permission or finish this course before using them. External legal channels also exist; this lesson does not give filing deadlines or case advice.

items.title: Manager action
items.body: A supervisor must immediately report the allegation or incident to HR or the AAO and follow agency procedures. They should not wait to see whether an optional conversation solves it. Assigned investigative duties remain governed by those procedures and authority.

items.title: Protection
items.body: A person should not be discouraged from reporting or punished for protected participation. A concern about retaliation belongs in the proper process. Record relevant facts through that channel rather than proving motive in a public learning activity.

tabs.label: Appropriate route
tabs.body: Describe the concern accurately and use the listed reporting process. Staff can take it seriously without declaring the final finding. The process determines what further information and authorized action are required.

tabs.label: Informal gate
tabs.body: Requiring a worksheet, consultant approval or confrontation with the person before accepting a report can create an improper barrier. Optional skill support does not override reporting routes or role responsibilities.

tabs.label: Course investigation
tabs.body: Asking classmates to examine a real allegation creates information and authority problems. Use the practice here. Actual investigative and corrective-action duties follow the agency’s assigned roles and procedures.

check.question: A supervisor receives a protected-class harassment allegation. What fits Policy 1436?
check.correct: Immediately report it to HR or the agency AAO and follow agency procedures.
wrong: Wait until the reporter completes a learning worksheet.
Require consultant approval before sending the report.
Declare that no supervisor may ever carry out an investigation assigned under agency procedures.
check.feedbackCorrect: This preserves the policy’s immediate reporting duty and authorized agency procedures.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Learning requirements and optional consultation cannot delay the reporting duty. The policy also preserves assigned investigation responsibilities under agency procedures; a blanket ban would misstate those roles.

sorting.heading: Reporting option, manager duty or improper barrier?

items.text: An employee reports a concern to agency HR.
An employee uses the agency AAO route.
A supervisor immediately reports the allegation to HR or the AAO.
A manager follows agency complaint and investigation procedures.
Require a consultant appointment before accepting a report.
Withhold a report until a course check is passed.

lessons.next: Next, combine the source, setting and responsible next step in a practical note.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A supervisor says they will hold an allegation until the team finishes this course.
options: The supervisor’s immediate HR or AAO reporting duty and agency procedures, without waiting for the course.
A course completion rule invented by the team.
A vote by classmates on whether the allegation is credible.
responses: This preserves the applicable responsibility and keeps the course separate.
The team cannot use an invented learning prerequisite to delay the duty.
A learning group is not the assigned investigation or decision process.

lessons.transfer: For a practice concern, identify the role, appropriate reporting route and a barrier to avoid.

move.control: You can recognize and use the proper process without a classroom finding.
move.failure: Optional learning becomes a prerequisite for reporting or a substitute investigation.
move.next: Practice the practice role distinction and keep actual records in their proper channel.

lessons.title: Apply the learning without overstating the conclusion
lessons.summary: Prepare a careful note and connect legal recognition to wider equity practice.
lessons.objective: Prepare a practice note identifying conduct, setting and relevant source.
objectives: Prepare a practice note identifying conduct, setting and relevant source.
State the limit between a concern and a final determination.
Explain that equity inquiry includes more than a protected-class checklist.
takeaways: A useful note identifies the issue and responsible next process.
Source awareness does not certify compliance or decide a case.
Equity work also examines access, power, perspectives and outcomes.
lessons.statement: Make the source and next responsibility clear, and keep the claim proportionate.

image.caption: A presenter points to a whiteboard chart while two colleagues discuss it at a table.

intro.heading: Recognition should support responsible action
intro.body:
A practical note can identify the conduct, relevant setting, source and next responsibility without becoming a legal brief. In the practice hiring case, the note might say that a comment connected marital status to expected retention and should be addressed through the appropriate employment process. It need not assert a final violation or assign the speaker a motive the learner cannot establish. In a service case, the note should identify the actual activity rather than copy the employment list automatically.

Use the direct source accurately. A statute, a state policy and a learning example are not interchangeable. The employer list, public-service list and public-accommodation list differ. Policy 1436 has its own wording and responsibilities. If the question involves an exception, another legal source or a specific person’s circumstances, state that authorized interpretation is needed. Do not present a course answer as permission to deny a service, waive eligibility or alter an employment decision.

Protected-class recognition is one part of equity work, not its entire scope. Staff can also examine whether an instruction is usable, whose knowledge informed a decision, who carries a burden and what the evidence shows about outcomes. An issue need not be declared unlawful in this course to merit a supported improvement inquiry. Equally, a general improvement discussion cannot replace a reporting duty or required formal analysis when it applies.

For the final practice, use a practice case or suitable draft and name the next responsible process. Keep actual records in their proper channels. Completing the course shows participation in learning; it does not establish approved mandatory training credit, certify legal compliance or prove that a real service is equitable. Clear boundaries allow the course to build useful recognition and practical capability without creating authority it does not hold.

inThisLesson: Connect recognition to broader equity inquiry.
State the next responsibility and limits.
lessons.keyStatement: The learning supports a responsible next step, not a universal legal or equity verdict.

flashcards.back: A concise description of the concern, setting, relevant source and next process.
An accurate separation of statute, policy and learning practice.
Examination of access, power, perspectives, effects and possible improvements.
The difference between completing learning and meeting actual legal, policy or training requirements.

items.title: Specific wording
items.body: Name the practice decision and statement rather than writing discrimination happened everywhere. The note can flag a serious concern while letting the proper process establish the facts and decision. This is not a demand that staff prove a legal case before reporting.

items.title: Accurate source
items.body: Say which provision or policy supplies the relevant list or responsibility. If the setting is uncertain, state the question instead of hiding it. An honest source limit is more useful than a confident but copied universal list.

items.title: Broader improvement
items.body: An access or participation problem may need analysis even when a classroom legal conclusion is unavailable. Examine the practical task and effects through appropriate procedures. Do not use the absence of a course verdict as proof that no equity concern exists.

tabs.label: Supported next step
tabs.body: The note identifies the concern and proper process with the relevant source. It states uncertainty without minimizing the issue or delaying an applicable role responsibility.

tabs.label: Compliance certificate
tabs.body: A course completion statement cannot certify the agency’s legal compliance, resolve an actual allegation or replace required analysis. The learning record and real operating responsibilities are distinct.

tabs.label: No inquiry needed
tabs.body: A protected-class checklist alone cannot establish that every person can use a service or that a process has equitable effects. Use appropriate evidence and affected perspectives to examine the broader task.

check.question: Which final statement is proportionate?
check.correct: The practice concern identifies a relevant source and next process; it does not establish the final legal finding or full compliance.
wrong: Passing the course certifies all workplace decisions as lawful.
If the class cannot decide a violation, no improvement question exists.
The learner may grant legal exceptions after reviewing a source list.
check.feedbackCorrect: This records useful recognition and preserves the boundaries of the course and actual procedures.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Learning completion is not a legal certificate, a decision authority or proof that every equity concern has been resolved. Use sources accurately, follow applicable responsibilities and keep broader inquiry tied to evidence.

sorting.heading: Useful note, equity inquiry or unsupported certification?

items.text: Identify the practice conduct, setting and relevant provision.
State the appropriate next process without a final finding.
Ask whether people can use the instruction and response route.
Examine whose perspectives informed a real open choice.
Passing this course certifies every legal obligation.
One copied list proves all outcomes are equitable.

lessons.next: Use the job aid to practice a careful note at your own pace.

scenario.context: DHS practice case: A summary says the team is fully compliant because everyone passed the protected-classes course.
options: Record the learning separately from actual legal and policy responsibilities, and preserve the appropriate operating reviews.
Treat the score as a final agency legal finding.
Stop all equity inquiry because the course is complete.
responses: This gives learning its proper role without overstating compliance or abandoning ongoing work.
A learning score cannot decide actual compliance.
Equity practice and applicable responsibilities continue beyond the course activity.

lessons.transfer: Write a practice note with conduct, setting, relevant source, responsible next process and uncertainty.

move.control: You can use protected-class knowledge to support responsible work.
move.failure: A course answer becomes an invented authority or universal compliance claim.
move.next: Practice with practice material or a suitable draft; do not disclose actual protected records.

jobAid.subtitle: Recognize the concern and use the proper process
remember: Protected-class lists depend on the provision and setting. Use direct sources, describe relevant conduct and follow the applicable responsibilities without making a course-based legal finding.

sections.heading: Identify the activity
items: Is the question about employment, a public service, a public accommodation or another setting?
Read the relevant provision and its conditions; the lists are not identical.
Other applicable law or policy may also matter.

sections.heading: Keep sources distinct
items: 363A.08 subdivision 2 supplies the employer list taught here.
363A.12 subdivision 1 supplies the public-services list; 363A.11 has a separate public-accommodations list.
Policy 1436 has its own wording, reporting options and role responsibilities.

sections.heading: Use definitions carefully
items: Do not infer identity or status from appearance.
Read definition conditions and context instead of applying an informal label.
A definition does not authorize unnecessary personal-information collection.

sections.heading: Preserve the proper route
items: Employees are encouraged to use Policy 1436’s reporting options for protected-class concerns.
Managers and supervisors must immediately report allegations or incidents to HR or the agency AAO and follow agency procedures.
Do not impose a course or consultant prerequisite, retaliate or replace assigned investigations with classroom discussion.

sections.heading: State the limit
items: A concern can be raised without the learner declaring a final finding.
Learning completion does not certify compliance or approved mandatory training credit.
Continue evidence-based equity inquiry and follow required processes for actual work.

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes 363A.03 — Definitions
sources.note: Relevant chapter definitions of characteristics, statuses and settings. Definitions and context should be checked in actual work.

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes 363A.08 — Employment
sources.note: Employer protections in subdivision 2 and related employment provisions. Do not treat the employer list as identical to every other chapter list.

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes 363A.12 — Public services
sources.note: Access to public services, the protected-class list and disability access provisions in subdivision 1.

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes 363A.11 — Public accommodations
sources.note: A separate statutory setting and protected-class list, with disability provisions. This course uses the distinction, not a complete legal analysis.

sources.title: Minnesota Statutes 363A.15 — Reprisals
sources.note: Reprisal protection for specified opposition, participation and association; statutory conditions remain relevant.

sources.title: MMB — Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited, Policy 1436
sources.note: Workplace and public-service-environment policy with its own protected-class definitions, reporting routes and manager responsibilities.
